chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Verily, the hearts of the ignorant are agitated by greed, held hostage by vain desires, and ensnared by deceptions.'

key_terms.الأطماع: Greed, covetousness — excessive desires for worldly gain
key_terms.الجهال: The ignorant — those lacking religious knowledge and spiritual discipline
key_terms.الخدائع: Deceptions, delusions — false beliefs and misleading temptations
key_terms.المنى: Vain hopes, wishful desires — illusions and unrealistic expectations

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the hearts of the ignorant?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) transmits a saying of Imam Ali (AS) diagnosing the spiritual condition of the ignorant: their hearts are perpetually enslaved by three forces — greed that restlessly drives them, empty desires that keep them captive, and deceptions that trap them. This hadith was addressed to communities in early Islamic society who lacked religious knowledge ('ilm), and the original audience would have understood 'ignorant' (juhhal) not merely as the intellectually unlearned, but as those who lack God-consciousness and discipline of the self.
word_analysis: and cling to them/attach to them

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘
The hearts of the ignorant ones trigger the greed, and the yearnings hold them hostage, and the deceptions attach to them’.
